requirements.statement: Audit scales, sheet definitions, pilot skills and injury rules against state and user-visible sheets.
requirements.reviewNote: The printed introduction was reviewed against the current scale constants, pilot data and record sheet. Existing tests establish concrete cases; this is an umbrella entry, not a claim of complete coverage. The remaining child requirements and scenario cross-references must be individually verified before closing foundations.

AGoAC pp.4-5: record sheet displays front and rear damage, current pilot skills and heat overflow

requirements.statement: Verify scenario setup and general deployment with initiative-selected opposite entry edges, walking/running/jumping entry and MP spent from the first complete hex.
requirements.reviewNote: Printed p.6 general setup: current Legacy.reset initializes all units inside the board at fixed coordinates; initiative goes directly to move and makeRuntime preserves that placement. The non-scenario initiative edge choice, opposite entry edges and border entry MP accounting are absent. Scenario-specific placement remains separate.

requirements.statement: Each side rolls independent 2D6; ties repeat; greater total wins and loser makes first selection.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.6: initiative handles every non-tied sum and rerolls all tied sums

requirements.statement: All six phases occur in order; pending selections cannot be skipped; new round begins following End.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.6-7: six-phase round and pending-order protection preserve state

requirements.statement: Use remaining-force ratios at the start of each declaration pair to determine batch sizes for unequal armies.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.7: unequal force batches match both printed examples and either initiative winner

requirements.statement: Undestroyed immobile and nonattacking units count for selections; declaration order and simultaneity, consciousness before PSRs, Heat and End actions and victory/draw conditions require independent audit.
requirements.reviewNote: Printed pp.6-7 and 30: buildQueue includes surviving immobile and unarmed units and declarations are stored. However resolveFire interleaves to-hit rolls with damage rather than an all-attacks-first stage; resolvePhysical processes charge declarations in unit-array order before other declarations; heat avoidance lacks an explicit conscious-pilot restriction; inherited checkWin handles last-side elimination but has no stalemate draw predicate. Split these into atomic follow-up implementation and regression requirements; do not infer complete timing from green CI. Follow-up separates ordinary weapon to-hit and ammo expenditure from damage and groups damage by target. Physical staging, selectable independent damage ordering, heat and stalemate remain outstanding. Thermal avoidance now distinguishes unconscious/unavailable pilots and automatic below-14 restart; voluntary shutdown/restart and phase PSR interactions remain independently auditable.

AGoAC p.7: unequal force batches match both printed examples and either initiative winner

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.4-5: record sheet displays front and rear damage, current pilot skills and heat overflow

requirements.statement: Standard Inner Sphere pilot defaults to Gunnery 4 and Piloting 5; those independent ratings drive the corresponding attack target numbers.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.5: base pilot defaults and skill-dependent attack targets

requirements.statement: Warrior Data shows the assigned pilot identity, skills, current wounds, consciousness and death state.

requirements.statement: Heat Data distinguishes total installed sinks from lost sinks in addition to the heat scale.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.5: Heat Data distinguishes installed and destroyed heat sinks

audit.review: Printed p.5 Heat Data explicitly tracks installed and damaged sinks. recordSheet uses installed count, lost count and one marked/unmarked dot per installed sink. The existing test iterates every loss value from no loss to all sinks lost. Rendering only; cooling, flooding and critical damage rules are separate.

requirements.statement: All combatant record sheets are public by default and can be inspected independently of the current tactical selection. Reviewed the three printed scenarios and their listed variations; no record-sheet secrecy exception is specified. Future custom scenario policy remains separate.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.4: inspecting enemy record sheet preserves active unit and target selection
AGoAC pp.4,45-48: every unit record remains open throughout all six battle phases

requirements.statement: Logical scale metadata is 30 m per hex, approximately 6 m per level, two levels for a standing chassis, and 10 s per complete turn. Range ignores elevation and is shortest horizontal hex distance; LOS and terrain movement effects are separate requirements.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.3-4,18: logical scale and shortest hex distance independent of height
AGoAC pp.6-7: six-phase round and pending-order protection preserve state

audit.review: Constants, completed-turn count, and axial distance were reviewed; breadth-first reference verifies all pairs on the existing board, including altered elevation. Existing six-phase test checks round advancement.

requirements.statement: Deferred consciousness rolls preserve the threshold of each individual wound; later checks stop after unconsciousness and sixth wound is lethal.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.6,44: delayed consciousness rolls retain each wound threshold

audit.review: Printed pp.6,44 distinguish attack-phase deferred checks, increasing wound-specific thresholds, stopping further rolls after unconsciousness and death at six. Game.wound and consciousness preserve the pending count and derive each original threshold, discard checks on death; existing test enumerates every nonlethal start/count and each possible first failure or full success, plus lethal sixth wound and JSON round trip. Immediate checks outside deferred attack resolution are covered separately.

requirements.statement: All phase-end consciousness checks precede all required piloting checks.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.6,44: all pilots roll consciousness before any phase PSR

requirements.statement: Recovery attempts begin in the following turn's end phase and use current accumulated wounds.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.44: recovery starts only in the next turn and uses current wounds
AGoAC pp.7,33,44: submerged life support wounds and lethal wounds cannot recover

audit.review: Printed pp.7,44: no recovery in the turn of loss, subsequent End Phase checks use current injury total and equality succeeds. endPhase uses wasUnconscious and the current conscious table index, updates the flag after the phase. Test exercises all five nonlethal injury counts, no same-turn RNG, failure one below threshold, then exact success; dead-pilot guard is also tested in submerged-life-support case. Scope is normal End Phase recovery, not all possible death/PSR interactions.

requirements.statement: One die consumes one RNG sample and maps to a face 1–6; a two-die roll consumes two separate samples, stores both faces and returns their sum. No assertion of cryptographic randomness.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.3: all six die faces and all 36 independent two-die combinations
BMM p.6: all 36 dice combinations obey inclusive target checks for TN -3 through 15

audit.review: Game.roll and Game.d6 use one RNG invocation per die; six faces and 36 ordered pairs checked, with 684 inclusive target comparisons as independent regression evidence.

requirements.statement: Each damaging head hit causes one wound even without internal damage.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.44: head hits wound the pilot even when armor holds

requirements.statement: An internal ammunition explosion inflicts two pilot wounds independent of armor.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.39,44: internal ammunition explosion wounds a surviving pilot twice

requirements.statement: Failed life support inflicts one wound at heat 15–25, two at 26 or more, and none below 15.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.33,39,44: damaged life support heat wounds at exact thresholds

audit.review: Printed pp.33,39,44 agree on life-support injury bands. heatPhase computes heat before applying the Boolean life-support critical condition and the 15/26 threshold branch. Regression covers both life-support states, zero, 14/15,25/26,30 and overflow 45 with other heat effects isolated; the branch is independent of voluntary shutdown and does not cumulative-double count. This certifies injury count for surviving pilot, not all heat timing/explosion interactions.

requirements.statement: With failed life support and full submersion, one wound occurs at end phase; a lethal sixth wound forbids further recovery.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.7,33,44: submerged life support wounds and lethal wounds cannot recover

audit.review: Printed pp.7,33,44 specify full submersion and End Phase wound; at six the warrior dies and cannot recover. endPhase checks depth against standing/prone thresholds, applies wound before recovery, skips dead units. The test covers life-support present/absent, standing/prone, depths 0–3, plus lethal sixth wound with no recovery RNG. Movement into water and hull-breach rules are separate.

requirements.statement: Seatbelt checks precede fall damage; target uses the original PSR modifiers and fall-height increment. Immobility or target above 12 causes automatic injury.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.43-44: fall seatbelt checks occur before damage with elevation modifiers
AGoAC pp.11,43-44: only genuine immobility makes seatbelt damage automatic

requirements.statement: Standing immobile chassis automatically fails required piloting checks; a prone chassis does not repeat them. Losing all limbs, reactor shutdown, abandonment and unconsciousness are classified independently of zero MP.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.11,40: standing limbless unit fails PSR automatically while prone unit need not roll

requirements.statement: All-limb loss provides the immobile target modifier and aimed-attack eligibility; head aiming replaces that modifier with +3. Full attack audit remains in the combat section.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.11,17,21: limb-loss immobility applies minus four and allows aimed head shots

requirements.statement: A rear-installed weapon is marked (R) beside its name in the critical hit table; the same label also appears in inventory. Firing arc behavior remains a separate combat requirement.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.5,15: rear-mounted weapon is identified in inventory and critical slots

audit.review: The record sheet uses the same weaponLabel helper for every weapon inventory row and every weapon critical slot, with one conditional based on rear mounting; positive and negative cases confirm both render paths.

requirements.statement: Show the base record sheet's separate critical damage counters for engine, gyro, sensors and life support, using accumulated critical state rather than temporary flooding.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.5: critical summary shows engine gyro sensors and life support hits

audit.review: Printed p.5 sample record-sheet summary contains three engine, two gyro, two sensor and one life-support mark. criticalSummary reads actual accumulated counters, not effectiveEngineHits or temporary flooding, and clamps to the printed capacities; all 72 combinations (4×3×3×2) are covered by the regression. Scope is displaying counters, not component effect implementation.

requirements.statement: Show ammunition magazine locations and capacity and remaining rounds separately in the critical hit table. Inventory aggregation and actual ammunition expenditure remain under combat.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.5: individual ammunition slots report capacity and remaining rounds

requirements.statement: Hexes without a terrain or level marking independently default to clear terrain and level zero. Store negative sublevels and water depth independently; preserve explicit terrain, level, and metadata across save/restore. Full terrain movement and LOS costs remain in their own sections.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.3-4: unmarked terrain and level default independently and survive map reload

requirements.statement: The record-sheet heat scale has levels 0–30, fills from low to high, identifies every effect breakpoint with a star and preserves an explicit overflow field above 30. Heat effect execution is audited separately.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.5,37-38: all heat scale levels mark effects and preserve current overflow

audit.review: Printed pp.5,37–38 specify heat scale 0–30, star-linked effects and overflow. heatScale implements exactly 31 levels and 17 breakpoints matched to the printed Heat Data table. Regression compares every label and star, order, fill and current marker for each heat 0–60, including exact overflow. This is displaying heat, not executing penalties.

requirements.statement: Warrior Data displays all six injury steps, accumulated wounds, the corresponding consciousness thresholds and death at six wounds.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.5,44: Warrior Data shows all six injury steps and the exact consciousness table

audit.review: Printed pp.5,44 Warrior Data table thresholds 3,5,7,10,11,death at six. warriorInjuryTable marks cumulative hits and current threshold; test compares every cell and all seven injury counts 0–6. Scope is the displayed table; injury causes, recovery and phase timing are separate.

requirements.statement: For each location, track every point of current and starting front armor and internal structure independently, with rear armor limited to the three torso sections.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.4-5: armor and structure dots track every section independently

evidence.test: AGoAC p.5: Mech Data uses actual chassis metadata with escaped text

requirements.statement: An unconscious pilot cannot give voluntary movement, weapon or physical orders, but the surviving Mech remains eligible for a pass selection.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.6,11,44: unconscious pilot cannot issue voluntary orders but can pass selections

requirements.statement: A Mech whose pilot dies is removed from the map at the end of that phase; preserve same-phase attack declarations and resolve occupancy and displacement until removal.
requirements.reviewNote: Printed pp.35 and 44 require phase-end map removal. Actual wound/destroyLocation marks dead immediately; movement occupancy and displacement ignore dead units before phase transition; the UI collapses a dead model but has no explicit phase-boundary removal state. Already-declared ordinary weapon attacks can still roll. Keep destruction and on-map presence distinct and audit displacement, immediate fall damage, persistence, and presentation together. Partial implementation in follow-up: standard lethal damage records pending phase-end map removal; historical state and ordinary attack declarations are retained. Full domino, fall, charge/DFA and simultaneous damage ordering remain to be independently audited. Keep known_missing until those interactions are covered. Ordinary weapon attack staging now spends ammunition and rolls all attacks before damage; pending verification in CI. Follow-up corrects ordinary charge into prohibited displacement terrain (pp.26,42): both units retain positions and damage/PSRs remain; lethal target is not displaced. Existing fractional charge-damage rounding is confirmed by the 65-ton/5-hex example. DFA alternatives, dominoes and physical interruption remain unresolved. Follow-up: opposed pushes resolve both attempts before any displacement, both successful attempts leave both positions unchanged and require immediate PSRs; prohibited push retains positions and requires PSR. Domino and accidental falls remain outstanding.

requirements.statement: For declared ordinary weapon fire, roll attacks and expend ammunition before resolving hit locations/damage; a destroyed shooter still completes its attacks, with damage grouped by target and packet.

evidence.test: AGoAC pp.6,21,30: every weapon attack rolls and spends ammo before damage, even a destroyed shooter
AGoAC pp.21,30: resolve each target and each missile packet completely in declared order

requirements.statement: A conscious pilot can attempt one highest-threshold thermal shutdown avoidance or restart roll at heat 14–29. An unconscious pilot cannot override thermal shutdown; an involuntarily shut-down reactor automatically restarts below 14 even if the pilot is out of action. Heat 30+ cannot be overridden.

evidence.test: AGoAC p.38: unconscious pilots cannot override thermal shutdown and auto restart below 14
AGoAC p.38: conscious pilot rolls only the highest thermal threshold and never at 30 or more
